title: Train station returning to Cheadle after more than 100 years

evidence_packet.title: Train station returning to Cheadle after more than 100 years
evidence_packet.lead: Cheadle in Stockport has been without a train station since its original hub closed in 1917
evidence_packet.summary: Cheadle in Stockport has been without a train station since its original hub closed in 1917
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Work is beginning on bringing a train station back to the heart of a Greater Manchester village more than a century after its original station closed Cheadle in Stockport had a station just off the high street up until 1917 Funding for a new hub, which would be built next to Alexandra Hospital, was given the green light in 2022, with planning permission granted in 2023 but concerns about its effect on the timetabling of trains elsewhere on the network led to delays Stockport Council said the issue had now been resolved and council leader Mark Roberts said it was "a hugely significant moment for Cheadle and for Stockport" "For years we've fought for this station because we know the difference it will make to residents, businesses and the future prosperity of the area," he added Roberts said he was delighted that the initial highways work could now start on site thanks to the persistence and partnership of all involved

title: Warrington teen to shave head to support mum with stage 4 cancer

evidence_packet.title: Warrington teen to shave head to support mum with stage 4 cancer
evidence_packet.lead: Henry is raising money for a hospice where his mum is undergoing palliative care
evidence_packet.summary: Henry is raising money for a hospice where his mum is undergoing palliative care
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A 13-year-old boy is having his head shaved to raise money for a hospice which is supporting his mum, who has stage four cancer Henry, from Warrington, Cheshire, decided he wanted to give back to St Rocco's Hospice in the town, which has been providing palliative care and support to his mum Sarah, 43, after she was diagnosed with bowel cancer about 18 months ago Henry said: "She has had multiple operations which were unsuccessful and she is now on palliative treatment to prolong her life "In the last few months St Rocco's has helped my mum to come to turns with this and will be more help in the future." He added: "With this in mind I want to raise money to help support them in continuing to provide the support and care to others like they have my mum." Sarah said she was "immensely proud of what he has achieved", describing Henry as "an amazing boy" and "such a caring loving young man"

title: Irish heritage and culture, as told by the women of the North West

evidence_packet.title: Irish heritage and culture, as told by the women of the North West
evidence_packet.lead: A new exhibition is celebrating the role of women in the rich Irish communities across northern England
evidence_packet.summary: A new exhibition is celebrating the role of women in the rich Irish communities across northern England
evidence_packet.evidence_text: North-west England has always had a rich and deep connection to Irish heritage, with Manchester, Lancashire - and Liverpool in particular - famed for its historic Irish communities Many families settled in the region after mass migration began from the mid-19th century during the Great Famine And with the boom of heavy industry - from shipbuilding and canal and road building in Liverpool to the mills of Manchester and Lancashire - by the 20th century, these areas became a heartland of Irish culture, including social clubs, folk music and the influence of the Catholic Still today the link persists, with the region being the most popular choice for Irish university students choosing to study overseas, according to the Department for the Economy , external But while Irish stories are weaved into the tapestry of the North West, some voices are quieter than others - leading two curators to ask: "Who are the women of Ireland in the North?" "Women don't get the space to have their voices heard," said Rosarie Walsh, a community interest company director, based in Trafford, in Greater Manchester

title: Homemade bomb part of alleged plot on Manchester's Jewish community, court told

evidence_packet.title: Homemade bomb part of alleged plot on Manchester's Jewish community, court told
evidence_packet.lead: Two men were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur, considered the holiest day in the Jewish calendar
evidence_packet.summary: Two men were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur, considered the holiest day in the Jewish calendar
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two Iranian men have appeared in court charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade bomb Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, were accused at Westminster Magistrates' Court of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism on or before 20 September One of the buildings they are alleged to have carried out reconnaissance at is the Heaton Park synagogue which was attacked on 2 October 2025 Both men, who had arrived in the UK by small boat, were arrested in Manchester's Northern Quarter on the eve of Yom Kippur - the holiest day in the Jewish calendar Salehi and Ahmadyan were remanded in custody by District Judge Nina Tempia until 23 October, when they will appear at the Old Bailey in London As part of the investigation, searches were carried out at addresses in Epworth Street, Liverpool, and Lancaster Road, Salford

Sinfield completed seven ultramarathons in seven days, crossing the finish line at Old Trafford Stadium in Manchester ahead of the Super League Grand Final. The fundraiser and his team have raised more than £13m for the MND community since his first annual challenge in 2020. Speaking to the crowd, Sinfield said: "The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob would be so proud to see how you've supported and cared, and showed your love for a community that really needs us." Sinfield began his final ultramarathon challenge in Hull on September 27 and visited all 12 Super League clubs along the way. The 7 in 7: The Grand Finale week ended at Old Trafford earlier where he brought out the trophy ahead of the game between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man from Liverpool has set himself the challenge of breaking a Guinness World Record for the fastest half marathon run by a man with multiple sclerosis (MS) Father-of-two David Price, 42, was diagnosed with MS in 2018 after starting to struggle with his balance and peripheral vision Eight years on, Price is preparing to attempt the record at the Manchester Half Marathon, but admits to feeling nervous The current record is held by Chris White, who achieved a time of 1 hour 30 minutes and 46 seconds in Brighton in March this year "It would mean the world to me to break the record," David said. title: From Molly-Mae to Gemma Collins - filming the real lives behind the headlines

evidence_packet.title: From Molly-Mae to Gemma Collins - filming the real lives behind the headlines
evidence_packet.lead: Creative director Demi Doyle opens up about what it is like to film behind the scenes
evidence_packet.summary: Creative director Demi Doyle opens up about what it is like to film behind the scenes
evidence_packet.evidence_text: When producer Demi Doyle was invited round to the home of Molly-Mae Hague to discuss the possibility of filming a new docuseries, she knew they needed to capture the highs, the lows and the beautifully mundane moments in between Demi had recently set up her own TV production company Navybee under the umbrella of the Manchester-based Workerbee Group, which is part of Banijay Entertainment "I just remember calling her agent Fran, who's amazing, and they were already wanting to do something on the wedding," said Demi, who had previously filmed Molly-Mae for the Netflix series At Home with the Furys "So this is when Tommy had proposed and I was like 'I would absolutely love to do it. Can you put me in the mix?'" Demi, from Ascot, travelled to her home to discuss the idea of letting cameras in, sharing their hopes for the series over a Chinese takeaway "If we're going to do it, we need to do it right," said the 33-year-old creative director, who is currently pregnant with her third child

title: Two men arrested in Eccles after £160k in cash found in cars

evidence_packet.title: Two men arrested in Eccles after £160k in cash found in cars
evidence_packet.lead: Men aged 37 and 51 are detained on suspicion of money laundering after two cars were stopped in Eccles
evidence_packet.summary: Men aged 37 and 51 are detained on suspicion of money laundering after two cars were stopped in Eccles
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two men have been arrested after about £160,000 was found in two cars travelling from Merseyside to Manchester Greater Manchester Police said it received reports of a suspicious vehicle at about 18:00 BST on Friday One vehicle stopped at the Eccles Interchange junction was found to have about £100,000 in cash inside. Shortly afterwards a second vehicle - also travelling to Manchester - was pulled over by police and £60,000 was seized Men aged 37 and 61 were arrested on suspicion of money laundering and both remain in custody for questioning Sgt Laura Abram said: "We will not tolerate any form of criminality on our streets – from driving offences to suspected money-laundering and associated criminality." title: Silsden father keeping son's memory alive by 'saving lives'

evidence_packet.title: Silsden father keeping son's memory alive by 'saving lives'
evidence_packet.lead: Michael Buckett has set up a mental health programme for schools in memory of his late son Ethan

evidence_packet.evidence_text: It is the post-midnight phone call that many parents of teenage children will be all too familiar with Michael Buckett's 19-year-old son Ethan would never ask directly for a lift home while stranded in Leeds - more than 20 miles away from home "He'd always send a message saying, 'What are you doing?'" evidence_packet.evidence_text: An investigation has been launched after a bus was seen travelling the wrong way on the M67 in Greater Manchester Witnesses reported seeing the double-decker Bee Network vehicle near Hattersley roundabout at about 05:45 BST on Friday Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) said there were no passengers on board at the time The bus operator, Metroline, is carrying out a full investigation Nick Fairclough, Transport for Greater Manchester's (TfGM) interim deputy director of bus, said there were no passengers on board and that the driver was assisted off the motorway safely. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A 13-year-old boy is having his head shaved to raise money for a hospice which is supporting his mum, who has stage four cancer Henry, from Warrington, Cheshire, decided he wanted to give back to St Rocco's Hospice in the town, which has been providing palliative care and support to his mum Sarah, 43, after she was diagnosed with bowel cancer about 18 months ago Henry said: "She has had multiple operations which were unsuccessful and she is now on palliative treatment to prolong her life "In the last few months St Rocco's has helped my mum to come to turns with this and will be more help in the future." title: Irish heritage and culture, as told by the women of the North West

evidence_packet.title: Irish heritage and culture, as told by the women of the North West
evidence_packet.lead: North-west England has always had a rich and deep connection to Irish heritage, with Manchester, Lancashire - and Liverpool in particular - famed for its historic Irish communities Many families settled in the region after mass migration began from the mid-19th century during the
evidence_packet.summary: North-west England has always had a rich and deep connection to Irish heritage, with Manchester, Lancashire - and Liverpool in particular - famed for its historic Irish communities Many families settled in the region after mass migration began from the mid-19th century during the
evidence_packet.evidence_text: North-west England has always had a rich and deep connection to Irish heritage, with Manchester, Lancashire - and Liverpool in particular - famed for its historic Irish communities Many families settled in the region after mass migration began from the mid-19th century during the Great Famine And with the boom of heavy industry - from shipbuilding and canal and road building in Liverpool to the mills of Manchester and Lancashire - by the 20th century, these areas became a heartland of Irish culture, including social clubs, folk music and the influence of the Catholic Still today the link persists, with the region being the most popular choice for Irish university students choosing to study overseas, according to the Department for the Economy , external But while Irish stories are weaved into the tapestry of the North West, some voices are quieter than others - leading two curators to ask: "Who are the women of Ireland in the North?" "Women don't get the space to have their voices heard," said Rosarie Walsh, a community interest company director, based in Trafford, in Greater Manchester

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two Iranian men have appeared in court charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade bomb Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, were accused at Westminster Magistrates' Court of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism on or before 20 September One of the buildings they are alleged to have carried out reconnaissance at is the Heaton Park synagogue which was attacked on 2 October 2025 Both men, who had arrived in the UK by small boat, were arrested in Manchester's Northern Quarter on the eve of Yom Kippur - the holiest day in the Jewish calendar Salehi and Ahmadyan were remanded in custody by District Judge Nina Tempia until 23 October, when they will appear at the Old Bailey in London As part of the investigation, searches were carried out at addresses in Epworth Street, Liverpool, and Lancaster Road, Salford

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sir Kevin Sinfield has completed his latest endurance challenge raising money for motor neurone disease (MND) causes in memory of his friend and teammate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024 Sinfield completed seven ultramarathons in seven days, crossing the finish line at Old Trafford Stadium in Manchester ahead of the Super League Grand Final The fundraiser and his team have raised more than £13m for the MND community since his first annual challenge in 2020 Speaking to the crowd, Sinfield said: "The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob would be so proud to see how you've supported and cared, and showed your love for a community that really needs us." evidence_packet.summary: Members of a criminal gang who smuggled almost £30m in cash from the UK to Dubai through airports including Manchester and Birmingham have been jailed Passing sentence at Bolton Crown Court, Judge Abigail Hudson described the offenders as a "shallow group of individuals" who "rev
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Members of a criminal gang who smuggled almost £30m in cash from the UK to Dubai through airports including Manchester and Birmingham have been jailed Passing sentence at Bolton Crown Court, Judge Abigail Hudson described the offenders as a "shallow group of individuals" who "revelled in spending obscene amounts of money" The judge said those involved were "fully aware and wholly disinterested" that the cash they were transporting came from serious criminal activity, often drug dealing The group used Emirates flights departing from Manchester, Birmingham and Brussels airports to transport criminal cash to the United Arab Emirates between 2017 and 2019 Sophie Logan, 31, formerly from Derby and living in Dubai at the time of the conspiracy, was jailed for seven years and six months The court heard Logan worked closely with the alleged organiser, helping arrange accommodation, meals and nights out for couriers who smuggled the money. Judge Hudson described her trial evidence as "entirely dishonest and evasive"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Thug stabbed ex-girlfriend's old partner in frenzied attack, telling him he was 'going to kill him over and over again' Aaron Law-Glindon 'behaved like an animal' News Amy Walker Court reporter 09:17, 03 Oct 2026 Updated 09:39, 03 Oct 2026 View A thug knifed his ex-girlfriend's old partner in a frenzied attack, 'telling him he was going to kill him over and over again'. Aaron Law-Glindon, 28, split with the woman in February 2024, though they continued to live together at her home She was on civil terms with another ex-boyfriend, who was visiting one day the following September. Manchester Crown Court heard Law-Glindon, from Timperley, Trafford, walked in before repeatedly punching the man in the head. He then went into the kitchen, grabbed 'one of the big He launched a further terrifying attack, swinging the blade at the man and stabbing him in the chest. Fortunately, the victim only needed stitches Law-Glindon was hauled before a judge this week for sentencing having previously admitted a charge of wounding. Recorder Imran Shafi KC told him: "Your actions that day were absolutely disgraceful. You behaved like an animal, which is doing a disservice to most animals." Following the hearing, Law-Glindon - who has dice tattooed on his hand - was pictured holding a lottery scratchcard after escaping an immediate prison sentence

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham How ‘Glastonbury for nerds’ introduced the nation to the real Andy Burnham “It's Andy who does the buses and now he's now he's got the nuclear codes.” View Image (Image: Andrew Stenning/Daily Mirror) It’s a comical assessment but one that passes muster given our new Prime Minister’s stratospheric rise to power over the last 12 months In September 2025, Andy Burnham was keeping a low profile at the Labour Party conference. So low in fact, that he wasn’t actually present at Sir Keir Starmer’s speech to avoid creating a distraction Speculation swirled about which seat he could take over to become an MP as friends encouraged him to challenge Starmer after setting out his stall in an interview with The New Statesman Starmer allies briefed that it all felt “a bit desperate”. But a year later, Mr Burnham sits in both Number 10 and Number 10 North It’s quite a story as Manchester Evening News journalists discuss in the latest Mancunian Way podcast episode. In it, we hear about Burnham’s storytelling abilities, his big promises and the silence that defined the most significant speech of his life

evidence_packet.title: Inside Stockport's new £6 million fire station where firefighters live out their 'childhood dream'
evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Inside Stockport's new £6 million fire station where firefighters live out their 'childhood dream' The Manchester Evening News was given an exclusive behind-the-scenes tour of the new state-of-the-art facility View 8 Images Station manager C News Chris Slater Senior Rep
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Inside Stockport's new £6 million fire station where firefighters live out their 'childhood dream' The Manchester Evening News was given an exclusive behind-the-scenes tour of the new state-of-the-art facility View 8 Images Station manager C News Chris Slater Senior Rep
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Inside Stockport's new £6 million fire station where firefighters live out their 'childhood dream' The Manchester Evening News was given an exclusive behind-the-scenes tour of the new state-of-the-art facility View 8 Images Station manager C News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 06:22, 04 Oct 2026 It's an iconic part of virtually every fire station. But for almost 60 years, there was no pole-drop at Stockport's central fire station The old building on King Street West, on the border of the town centre and Edgeley , which opened in the 1960s, was single-storey, so there was no need for one "Most crews have worked here at Stockport all their careers, and they'd never been to a pole drop station," said station manager Carl Petch Now all that has changed with the opening of the state-of-the-art new £6 million facility, which has just opened on the same site as the previous one Now spanning two floors, the firefighters based here now have the opportunity to recreate the scene so many people associate with the job

It has stirred up excitement on both sides of the Pe News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 06:22, 04 Oct 2026 Updated 07:38, 04 Oct 2026 Walking through the village of Hollingworth, you’d be forgiven for thinking ‘I could do without all those HGVs rattling past’. Imagine living there To put it into the words of 77-year-old Brenda Hardy - ‘it’s chaos’. The village sits on the Greater Manchester border with Derbyshire and has the pleasure of being the thoroughfare to Sheffield for juggernauts too big to go on the Snake Pass Traffic has been a problem in the not-so-sleepy village for decades. This is because you have to pass through to get onto Woodhead Pass (A628), if you exceed the 7.5 tonne weight limit to go on the Snake Pass The solution to the problem, the Mottram bypass, is actually under construction down the road . But the bypass ends right on the doorstep of Hollingworth and pays them zero benefit So when the idea that could sort the issue - a 14-mile tunnel under the Pennines - came about, there was excitement. I'm running a mar
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Health and fitness The daft Sunday morning decision that brought me seven months of pain and joy The benefits have been immense - and I've been able to help someone I love dearly News opinion Todd Fitzgerald Executive editor 06:21, 04 Oct 2026 View 3 "That's it. I'm running a marathon." I didn't really believe myself that rainy Sunday morning as I came out with the words that would change my life over the next seven months Ever so slightly hungover, I had a vague plan to drag myself out of bed and go for a jog. I'd run casually for a year or two, but nothing beyond five or six miles and with no real commitment I don't know why I said it. I don't know why I woke up even thinking it. But that - probably daft - decision would shape my existence in ways I'd never have imagined in 2026 A quick Google search and I settled on the Chester Marathon. It was only March. October 11 was ages away. Plenty of time... I hoped I booked a hotel in the city with my partner and by the time I was brushing my teeth, that was that. I ran 3.01 miles that morning. Pretty pathetic considering what was to come

"Britain's answer to New Kids On The Block. Here they are, it's Take That ." It's Halloween night 1990 and Gary, Mark, Howard, Jason and Robbie are making their debut TV appearance live on the old Granada clubbing show Hitman and Her . But while Strachan might have been right about Take That's future prospects, it's been a much different story for the clu The old Theatre Royal has now stood empty for almost 20 years as uncertainty surrounds its future. And campaigners are getting worried The Peter Street venue began life in 1844 when the city's existing royal theatre, on Fountain Street, was destroyed in a fire. Sensing an opportunity, local entrepreneur John Knowles bought the site of the Wellington Hotel, levelled it and set about building a replacement

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rugby League Rugby legend Sir Kevin Sinfield completes massive charity challenge before watching his son clinch Super League title The former Leeds Rhinos star has been running an ultramarathon every day Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter an Rugby legend Sir Kevin Sinfield completed his latest charity challenge by bringing the Super League trophy into a sold-out Old Trafford , before his son helped Wakefield to clinch the title The former Leeds Rhinos star, from Oldham , has been running an ultramarathon every day since September 27 to raise money for the MND Foundation, visiting each of the home grounds of the 12 English Betfred Super League clubs. He arrived from St Helens on the final day of his 7 in The number 7 is in honour of the late Rob Burrow CBE, another Leeds Rhinos legend who wore the number and sadly passed away from the disease in 2024 after living with it for over four years. Wakefield beat Warrington Wolves 23-10 in tonight's final, with Sir Kevin's son Jack scor The 46-year-old, a seven-time winner of the prestigious trophy as a player, said: “It’s great to be back. Thank you to everybody who’s played a part this week “The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob (Burrow) would be so proud to see how you’ve shown love and cared for a community that really needs us.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Two Iranian men to appear in court charged with suspected terror plot against Manchester's Jewish community - full charges and details Salam Ahmadyan, 36, of Liverpool, and Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, are both charged with engaged in conduct Two Iranian men are due to appear in court accused of an alleged plot against Manchester's Jewish community. Salam Ahmadyan, 36, of Liverpool; and Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, were arrested on Newton Street in the Northern Quarter on September 20 They were charged, on Friday (October 2), with engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts, contrary to Section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006 on the eve on Yom Kippur, Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) said Specialist counter terror cops from the Metropolitan Police in London descended on Newton Street before a second swoop at a hostel on Lancaster Road in Salford and a raid on a flat in Liverpool The defendants, who both arrived in the UK via small boat several years ago, are due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Saturday (October 3) An earlier CPS statement read: "The Crown Prosecution Service has announced two men have been charged with engaging in conduct in preparation of acts of terrorism in Greater Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Thug stabbed ex-girlfriend's old partner in frenzied attack, telling him he was 'going to kill him over and over again' Aaron Law-Glindon 'behaved like an animal' News Amy Walker Court reporter 09:17, 03 Oct 2026 Updated 09:39, 03 Oct 2026 View A thug knifed his ex-girlfriend's old partner in a frenzied attack, 'telling him he was going to kill him over and over again'. Aaron Law-Glindon, 28, split with the woman in February 2024, though they continued to live together at her home She was on civil terms with another ex-boyfriend, who was visiting one day the following September. Manchester Crown Court heard Law-Glindon, from Timperley, Trafford, walked in before repeatedly punching the man in the head. He then went into the kitchen, grabbed 'one of the big He launched a further terrifying attack, swinging the blade at the man and stabbing him in the chest. Fortunately, the victim only needed stitches Law-Glindon was hauled before a judge this week for sentencing having previously admitted a charge of wounding. Recorder Imran Shafi KC told him: "Your actions that day were absolutely disgraceful. You behaved like an animal, which is doing a disservice to most animals." Following the hearing, Law-Glindon - who has dice tattooed on his hand - was pictured holding a lottery scratchcard after escaping an immediate prison sentence

But when challenged the 67-year-old claimed he was looking for a dog he thought had been knocked down Not believing his story, the husband and wife farmers checked their CCTV and saw Brooks and another unidentified man entering an unlocked outhouse. They asked him directly if he had stolen anything but he was 'adamant that he had not' Brooks then fled in a car and the farmers discovered a welder, a grinder, a saw and a cordless drill worth around £580 had been stolen. Police traced the pensioner through his car registration and eight days later - on October 18, 2023 - he attended the police station for a volun Appearing at Preston Crown Court in August this year, Brooks, of Lockside, Blackburn, Lancs, admitted one count of burglary. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rugby League Rugby legend Sir Kevin Sinfield completes massive charity challenge before watching his son clinch Super League title The former Leeds Rhinos star has been running an ultramarathon every day Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter an Rugby legend Sir Kevin Sinfield completed his latest charity challenge by bringing the Super League trophy into a sold-out Old Trafford , before his son helped Wakefield to clinch the title The former Leeds Rhinos star, from Oldham , has been running an ultramarathon every day since September 27 to raise money for the MND Foundation, visiting each of the home grounds of the 12 English Betfred Super League clubs. He arrived from St Helens on the final day of his 7 in The number 7 is in honour of the late Rob Burrow CBE, another Leeds Rhinos legend who wore the number and sadly passed away from the disease in 2024 after living with it for over four years. Wakefield beat Warrington Wolves 23-10 in tonight's final, with Sir Kevin's son Jack scor The 46-year-old, a seven-time winner of the prestigious trophy as a player, said: “It’s great to be back. Thank you to everybody who’s played a part this week “The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob (Burrow) would be so proud to see how you’ve shown love and cared for a community that really needs us.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton 'We don't ever want our boy to be in the position where needs somebody else's heart' "The fear in our body is unreal" News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 20:45, 03 Oct 2026 View 3 Images George Kenny has a heart condition The mother of a 10-year-old boy described her fear as 'unreal' after her son suddenly suffered a cardiac arrest while having fun in a playground George Kenny was rushed to hospital on following the incident on September 22. The schoolboy from Bolton has an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) fitted underneath his skin - but his mum told the Manchester Evening News it was unable to shock his heart back to regulari "He's in hospital and he will be for a couple of weeks," said Kimberley Kenny, George's mum. "His consultant said if it does happen again, he will need to go on the transplant list. The realisation that he will need a transplant is daunting "The fear in our body is unreal. We don't ever want him to be in that position where needs somebody else's heart "For another family to go through that situation where their loved one's passed away and their organs are being sent away to save someone else's life is awful to be in."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Little Hulton Investigation launched into 'strong and unpleasant' smell lingering around Salford town "People are fed up because there's no real change" News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 18:45, 03 Oct 2026 View Image Little Hulton residents have repo An investigation has been launched after Salford residents complained of a 'bad smell' that is terrorising their neighbourhood. The Environment Agency says it is looking into reports of the 'odour' in Little Hulton Jordan Newman has lived in the area for 15 years. He told the Manchester Evening News the stench which smells like 'rotten eggs' has been prevalent in the town for years "This bad smell in Little Hulton isn't something new," he said. "It's been going on for years. It comes and goes depending on which way the wind is blowing, and when it hits, it's really strong and unpleasant right across the area "Lots of us have reported it to the Environment Agency time and time again. Every time we do, we get the same reply; that the site responsible will be moving soon. But nothing changes "The smell keeps coming back, and we keep getting told the same thing, over and over. She paid tribute to City after describing how one incid Natalie told how she then faced her stalker in court, and laid bare how his actions had led to 'one of the hardest periods' of her life. She said she was speaking out to offer support to anyone going through a similar experience On Facebook, Natalie said: "At the end of September, an individual was sentenced after pleading guilty to stalking me, involving serious alarm or distress. The court imposed a custodial sentence, suspended, alongside other requirements and a restraining order preventing him from "For eight months, this has been something I have had to deal with alongside every other part of my life, and at times it has been incredibly difficult. I hope this marks the end of one of the hardest periods of my life and allows me to finally close this chapter and move forward

Salam Ahmadyan, 36, of Liverpool; and Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, were arrested on Newton Street in the Northern Quarter on September 20 They were charged, on Friday (October 2), with engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts, contrary to Section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006 on the eve on Yom Kippur, Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) said Specialist counter terror cops from the Metropolitan Police in London descended on Newton Street before a second swoop at a hostel on Lancaster Road in Salford and a raid on a flat in Liverpool The defendants, who both arrived in the UK via small boat several years ago, are due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Saturday (October 3) An earlier CPS statement read: "The Crown Prosecution Service has announced two men have been charged with engaging in conduct in preparation of acts of terrorism in Greater Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Life-long crook was caught red-handed then tried to claim his dog had been run over Christopher Brooks has more 30 convictions in a 50-year life of crime View Image Christopher Brooks (Image: Lancs Police) News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:51, 03 Oct 2026 An elderly crook was caught red-handed stealing from a family farm - then tried to cover his tracks by claiming his dog had been run over Christopher Brooks was spotted by the owners of Walleach Farm at Turton in Bolton as he tried to flee the scene, a court heard. But when challenged the 67-year-old claimed he was looking for a dog he thought had been knocked down Not believing his story, the husband and wife farmers checked their CCTV and saw Brooks and another unidentified man entering an unlocked outhouse. They asked him directly if he had stolen anything but he was 'adamant that he had not' Brooks then fled in a car and the farmers discovered a welder, a grinder, a saw and a cordless drill worth around £580 had been stolen. Police traced the pensioner through his car registration and eight days later - on October 18, 2023 - he attended the police station for a volun Appearing at Preston Crown Court in August this year, Brooks, of Lockside, Blackburn, Lancs, admitted one count of burglary. The court heard he had 33 previous convictions for 66 offences, largely for theft, burglary and handling stolen goods, in a near 50-year criminal career

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Gang tried to smuggle £11m worth of 'pink cocaine' to Australia Four men have now been jailed Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 20:11, 02 Oct 2026 View 3 Images The 'pink cocaine' was stamped with Pink Panther logos (Image: NCA) A gang tried to smuggle almost £11 million worth of 'pink cocaine' to Australia Liverpool based Lee Brittles, 47, and fellow criminal Teo Grbesic, 23, tried to move the huge load of the drug, which does not actually contain cocaine but a mixture of MDMA, ketamine and caffeine, to the other side of the world The load was addressed to Castle Hill, a suburb of Sydney, and was hidden within an industrial bench cutting saw. But police moved in after being alerted by a suspicious driver. The drugs were said to have a street value of £11.3 million in the UK, and $57m down under Brittles and other accomplices made eight further bids to export drugs to Australia and New Zealand, including through Manchester Airport . But Brittles, Grbesic and two other men have now been jailed The National Crime Agency said in a statement: "On 10 October 2024, Brittles and Grbesic dropped off the drugs, which weighed 252.8kg and were stamped with Pink Panther logos, to a Fed Ex driver in Liverpool. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The WhatsApp group that hid a dark truth at Manchester Airport The full story of how a £22m dirty cash smuggling scheme came crashing down View 11 Images "This crime group smuggled enormous quantities of cash" News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19:37, 02 Oct 2026 Posing as holidaymakers, they would arrive at Manchester Airport and check in on Emirates flights, for what they claimed were short breaks in the ever-popular surroundings of Dubai However, the truth was much more sinister. They were, in fact, criminals who had become 'obsessed' with living a luxury lifestyle, leading a judge to label them some of the most 'shallow' people she had ever encountered Inside their suitcases, concealed inside clothes, were bundles of dirty cash they were smuggling into the UAE. It was all part of an ‘industrial scale’ cross-border scheme in which millions of pounds were being laundered for criminals, including ‘high-level’ drug dealers 'At the heart' of the operation was a British Dubai-based kingpin, alleged to be the 'controlling mind.' A judge said he had 'chosen not to face the court.' He is 'awaiting extradition to the UK to face trial,' the National Crime Agency (NCA) said. He cannot be identified for leg Members of the gang were put up in expensive Dubai hotels and had meals and visits to expensive nightclubs and beach clubs paid for. However, sometimes they were in the city state for just a matter of hours before catching return flights to pick up more cash

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred vans, and the doors swing open. Out from within comes cart after cart full of corn This is the not-entirely-secret HQ of the Market Street corn vendors: a four-storey council-owned car park, sitting across two of Manchester’s busiest streets. When I get there, the men are working in silence, hands sheathed in black gloves, bags of sweetcorn torn open, cardboard Just as I’m about to approach a vendor, I’m forwarded an email from a reader. It has the subject line The Mystery We All Want Solved "The reason I’m writing is because the people of Manchester are desperate to know what the hell is going on with all of the corn sellers on Market St "Why are there now so many of them? How on earth do they make a profit? Are they independent vendors or all part of the same company? Is their presence legal? What does their proliferation say about the state of the city centre?”

evidence_packet.summary: Passing sentence at Bolton Crown Court, Judge Abigail Hudson described the offenders as a "shallow group of individuals" who "revelled in spending obscene amounts of money" The judge said those involved were "fully aware and wholly disinterested" that the cash they were transport
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Passing sentence at Bolton Crown Court, Judge Abigail Hudson described the offenders as a "shallow group of individuals" who "revelled in spending obscene amounts of money" The judge said those involved were "fully aware and wholly disinterested" that the cash they were transporting came from serious criminal activity, often drug dealing The group used Emirates flights departing from Manchester, Birmingham and Brussels airports to transport criminal cash to the United Arab Emirates between 2017 and 2019 Sophie Logan, 31, formerly from Derby and living in Dubai at the time of the conspiracy, was jailed for seven years and six months The court heard Logan worked closely with the alleged organiser, helping arrange accommodation, meals and nights out for couriers who smuggled the money. Judge Hudson described her trial evidence as "entirely dishonest and evasive" Heather Jeffrey, 58, from Bradford, was jailed for six years and six months, while Devanyl Graham, 27, from Dewsbury, received a six-year sentence

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humani Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a stor Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. event.event_name: Beat the Jams Autumn season announced

evidence_packet.title: Beat the Jams Autumn season announced
evidence_packet.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Four Manchester kitchens close the season with an eight-course menu of cedar-smoked salmon, jerk monkfish, Greek lamb and Jose Cuervo cocktails Go to Manchester's Finest X profile After a summer of brilliant dinners at Torr Vale Mill, Open Fire Dining Club is closing the season with an all-star service On 26 and 27 September , Tartuffe will be joined by A-Kin, Portfolio and Kallos for a final eight-course menu that brings together four very different parts of Manchester’s food scene It feels like the right way to end the season. A-Kin founded by long-time friends Gasim and Sean, have become one of the city’s most exciting supper club names, turning dinners into nights built around food, music and conversation. Portfolio brings Julian Pizer back to the grills Tartuffe , as ever, will be holding the whole thing together from the grills, starting with oysters and venison, bringing in a seasonal nectarine gazpacho, and finishing their side of the menu with Alp Blossom cheese and elderberry honey before Kallos take things into dessert Tartuffe start things off with an oyster dressed with beef fat, wasabi and XO. It’s already something of a house classic, and won Best Dressed Oyster at Manchester Oyster Festival 2026. The beef fat comes from Cheshire cattle, aged and smoked before being worked into the dish

evidence_packet.summary: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, back
evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Childhood friends ‘choose Manchester over Silicon Valley’ Posted on October 2, 2026 by staff Childhood friends ‘choose Manchester over Silicon Valley’ Y Combinator founders George Jefferson and Art Freebrey, aged 21, raise $3m to build AI marketing startup Revnu Share: Listen to article Founders Investment MarTech Two 21-year-old childhood friends have raised $3 million for an AI platform designed to help growing businesses find customers and build their sales pipelines without the cost of a large in-house marketing team. Revnu was founded by George Jefferson and Art Freebrey, who first met in secondary school before going on to launch a string of businesses together while still in education. Their early ventures included software to automate the buying and selling of rare vintage clothes and trainers, before they went on to build an accounting platform for Vinted sellers. While at university, their businesses were generating around $15,000 a month. After recognising that the AI systems they had developed to automate work in their own businesses could have a much wider application, George and Art were encouraged by Monzo co-founder Jonas Templestein to pursue the opportunity and apply to Y Combinator. The pair then dropped out of university and moved temporarily to Silicon Valley to take part in the renowned accelerator. Revnu has now raised $3m in a round led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II. The company also received backing from Y Combinator. evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester’s first new train station of the 21st century is now being built, reconnecting Golborne near Wigan to the railway network for the first time in more than 60 years Set to open in spring 2028, the new station will be served by an hourly service between Wigan and
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester’s first new train station of the 21st century is now being built, reconnecting Golborne near Wigan to the railway network for the first time in more than 60 years Set to open in spring 2028, the new station will be served by an hourly service between Wigan and Stalybridge, via Manchester Victoria. It’s good news for the town which currently has no direct bus, train or tram services to Manchester. It is expected to reduce journey times from The station will have step-free access throughout, plus a new footbridge across the tracks and lifts to both platforms. The car park next to the station will be resurfaced and given upgraded lighting and CCTV, while walking, wheeling and cycling routes between the town centre and Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig visited the site. She said, “People in Golborne have been crying out for better transport links. We’ve listened and we’re building a brand-new train station that will reconnect the community to the rail network for the first time in more than “It’s a big moment for Greater Manchester too – our first new train station in more than 25 years – and I can’t wait to board the first trains stopping here. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Defoe’s deadly finishing, particularly earlier in his career for the likes of West Ham and Tottenham , led to interest from several big Premier League clubs United, then the dominant force in the league under Sir Alex, were among the interested parties, first during his stint in east London , prior to his 2004 move to north London, and later when he played for Tottenham. Defoe claims United players were even discussing him as a poten The 43-year-old revealed that ex-United defender Patrice Evra recently asked him why he never signed for the Reds. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Man City latest: Damning evidence against 115 charges appeal as whistleblower goes into hiding Manchester City have appealed the guilty verdict delivered by the independent commission - but a key part of their defence may be in tatters Comments S Manchester City were found guilty by an independent commission of all but one of the charges brought against them by the Premier League. The club was found guilty of operating a scheme to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by nearly £1billion across a nine-season peri The commission ruled against City on every count of breaching financial regulations between 2009-10 and 2017-18, concluding that the club used "sham" commercial deals to disguise owner funding and arrangements to reduce operating costs, such as coaching staff and player wages Premier League chief executive Richard Masters described the case, and its outcome, as "the most significant in Premier League history". The same commission will now deliberate over sanctions at a separate hearing, should City's appeal be unsuccessful Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! evidence_packet.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
